paper.title: Hybrid machine learning data assimilation for marine biogeochemistry

methods.architecture_note: Fully connected ANN tuned by AutoKeras (100 trials) that predicts state-dependent background correlations between total chlorophyll and unobserved variables; the correlations feed an OI/Kalman-type update with climatological variances. Network classified on itself (rule 5), coupling to the DA scheme recorded here.

evidence.quote: Each ML model is a fully connected ANN optimized using AutoKeras

methods.canonical_name: ML-EtE (end-to-end machine learning of EnKF updates)
methods.architecture_note: Fully connected ANN tuned by AutoKeras (100 trials) that emulates the EnKF analysis increments of unobserved variables from the background state and the total chlorophyll increment; replaces only the analysis step, not the forecast model.

evidence.quote: Each ML model is a fully connected ANN optimized using AutoKeras

methods.architecture_note: Updates only total chlorophyll (and PFTs by stoichiometry) with climatological background variances; no learned parameters.

evidence.quote: Its purpose is to mimic existing DA systems used by several operational centres

methods.architecture_note: Ensemble-based flow-dependent covariances, no learned parameters; also generates training data for ML-EtE.

evidence.quote: The stochastic EnKF scheme, see e.g., Evensen (2003)

methods.architecture_note: Same update as ML-OI but with purely climatological correlations from the EnKF run.

evidence.quote: A further non-ML-based scheme is used to update the extended range of variables

datasets.canonical_name: Synthetic GOTM-FABM-ERSEM ensembles at L4 (English Channel)

evidence.quote: is a highly biologically productive site with seasonally stratified dynamics
We generate training samples at seven day intervals across these free-runs

datasets.canonical_name: Synthetic GOTM-FABM-ERSEM ensembles at CWEC (Central Western English Channel)

evidence.quote: Besides the L4 site, we configure a setup for an additional location

experiments.note: Offline correlation prediction and online cycled DA, nitrate only. Training setup (loss, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, hardware) is not given for any ML model; only an AutoKeras search over 100 trials is described (p9).

results.metric_raw: RMS difference to true chlorophyll-nitrate correlation
results.quote: the ML model ( RMSE = 0.255) vastly outperforms the climatological statistics estimates (RMSE = 0.731)

results.metric_raw: relative improvement of correlation RMSE over climatology
results.config: offline, 3-year test period, ML-OI vs climatology

limitations.quote: The availability of a reanalysis is a clear obstacle of this approach
SHAP is somewhat limited in the presence of highly correlated features
in practice its extendability to a new location is limited by both availability of training data and to the new location
it is easy to hypothesise that the ML models have overfitted to L4
A limitation of our two test locations is that they are not directly coupled
